tools.description: Record the classified instrument model and report type for this scanned service document.

instrument_serial.description: Serial number as printed, or empty if none

task_code.description: Work Order Task Code as printed (e.g. T113), or empty

work_order_number.description: Work-order number as printed, or empty

content.text:
This is a scanned BD Care service report for one flow cytometer in a fixed fleet of three models. Identify three things and report a confidence (0 to 1) for each independently — they are not the same call.

1. Which instrument model this document is for. Look for the "Installed Product" or "System" field, which prints a code and model name (e.g. "648282B3 - ARIA III ACDU 6B/3R/3V" is a FACSAria III; "665158 - FACSDiscover S8 ..." is a FACSDiscover S8). Only choose from the allowed options.

2. What kind of service visit this is. The most reliable signal is the "Work Order Task Code" field: a code starting T113 ("Repair / Troubleshooting Visit") means repair; a code starting T111 ("Preventive Maintenance") means preventive_maintenance; a code starting T107 ("Install: Options, Upgrades, S/W") means installation_upgrade; anything referencing CS&T/QC calibration with no fault or PM-kit language means calibration. Repair, PM, installation and calibration visits otherwise share the same generic form layout, so this is a genuinely harder call than #1 — give it a lower confidence when the task code is unclear or missing rather than guessing high. Separately, copy the Work Order Task Code exactly as printed (e.g. "T113") into `task_code` with a `task_code_confidence`; the application maps the code to a report type itself, so accuracy of the characters matters more than your interpretation of them. If there is no task code, return an empty string with confidence 0.

3. The instrument's serial number, exactly as printed in the "Installed Product" block (its "Serial/Lot Number" line, e.g. "MP6651580000057"). Ignore the "Serial/Lot Number: N/A" line under the SYSTEM column, which is not the instrument's. Copy the characters exactly; never guess or complete a character you cannot read — give a lower confidence instead. If the Installed Product has no serial number, or it is printed as N/A, return an empty string with confidence 0.

4. The work-order number, exactly as printed (e.g. "WO-04587090"), in `work_order_number`; an empty string if the document shows none.

Give confidence scores that reflect real uncertainty. A clean, legible, unambiguous read deserves something like 0.9-0.98. Anything you had to infer rather than read directly, or where the document is ambiguous between two categories, deserves meaningfully lower — do not default to a high number out of politeness.

tools.name: record_extraction
tools.description: Record the extracted value and confidence for every field of this report template.

content.text:
This is a scanned BD Care service report. Extract exactly the fields listed in the tool schema below, and only those fields — nothing else on the page.

For each field, give:
- `value`: read directly from the document. If the field's content genuinely isn't present on the form, use an empty string ("" for text, [] for lists, or the type's natural empty value) rather than inventing something, and give it a low confidence.
- `confidence`: 0 to 1, reflecting how sure you actually are — a clean, unambiguous, directly-printed value deserves 0.85+; anything inferred, illegible, or genuinely absent from the form deserves meaningfully lower. Don't default to a high number.

Privacy — this is not optional: never let the customer's name, account, address, phone number, contract number, or any other contact/billing detail enter a field's value, even in a text field, even when that detail sits on the same line or right next to text you do need. This also covers the engineer/technician's own name and the date they signed or logged an entry — quote logs are often written as "<note>. By <name> on <date>", and that attribution is not part of the fault, work, or note content any field is asking for. Crop tightly to only the content the field actually asks for. For example, a Subject line reading "11 Month Recurring / SMX0457374" contains a contract number after the slash — extract only "11 Month Recurring". Likewise a quote reading "Air bubble in bleach line. By Shachar on 18/04/2021" contains a technician sign-off — extract only "Air bubble in bleach line".

Separately from the template's fields, also give `report_date`: the date this service visit was carried out, as YYYY-MM-DD. This is the one date the record itself needs — the privacy rule above is about keeping dates out of *field values*, not about this. On a BD Care Work Order Service Report, take it from the LABOR table's Start/End Date And Time — the day the engineer actually worked on the instrument (if labor spans several days, use the last End date). If there is no labor table, use the date printed beside the signatures. Never use the service contract start/end dates, the PO date, or any date in the CALIBRATED TOOLS table — those describe the contract and the engineer's test equipment, not this visit.

BD forms are not consistent about day/month order: some print dates month-first (02/10/2026 is 10 February 2026), others day-first (18/04/2021 is 18 April 2021). Every date on one form uses the same order, so work it out from this form: any date on the page with a part greater than 12 settles it (03/17/2025 can only be month-first). If nothing on the form settles it, give your best reading and a `report_date__confidence` of 0.5 or lower. If no visit date appears on the form, use an empty string with a low confidence.

Fields to extract:
- fault_description (text) — reported symptom (BD's Subject line + Description)
- root_cause (text) — matches the form's own "Cause" section
- work_performed (text) — diagnostic/repair narrative ("Work Performed / Solution Comments")
- components_replaced (object[]) — one entry per part; mirrors the form's "Parts Used" table
- labor_hours (number, unit: hours) — rounded total from the form's "Labor" line
- fault_category (enum) — technician-assigned, not on the source form
- retest_result (enum) — technician-assigned, not on the source form

input.fault_description: Stream is unstable with all nozzles - ARIA III S/N P648282B3003. Stream is unstable with all nozzles.
input.root_cause: Stream is moving down and fsc ssc position shifts
input.work_performed:
November 10, it took a while to identify the issue. The stream position suddenly moved up and down. Replaced the ball seal and checked that there is no air leakage from the sample chamber. Replaced the sheath regulator. After replacing the sheath regulator, no stream instability was noticed. Calibrated the sample and sheath regulators for 3psi and 75psi, then proceeded with the sample flow rate adjustment, but ran out of time.

November 11, calibrated the sample flow rate. All optics then had to be recalibrated. Cleaned the flow cell internally and externally, and began aligning the optics. Performed one CST on nozzle 100 and found the violet laser CV was 5.6 (passed, but not satisfactory). Noticed event rate with the 100 µm nozzle was high (~800 events). Attempted to recalibrate flow rate but it was unstable and fluctuating a lot.

November 12, while trying to calibrate sample flow rate, noticed the sample regulator was not operating properly — event rate spiked to ~2000 when going from nozzle 70 to 100, dropping to 350 when offset lowered by 1. Only one spare regulator was available, so reinstalled the original sheath regulator and replaced the sample regulator instead. Redid sample and sheath regulator calibration for 3psi and 75psi. Event rate fluctuated ±100 but sample rate calibration was completed. Stream sometimes became unstable again, and occasionally uploading a tube gave 0 events, resolved only by stopping and restarting the stream. After the last flow rate calibration, optics had to be recalibrated again — all lasers but the violet were successfully aligned; violet laser CV could not be calibrated below 6.5-6.8 despite adjusting the fiber manipulator position and rotating the fiber in the kinematic mount. Suspected the fluidics issue was affecting the violet laser.

November 18, inflated the sheath tank and checked for pressure loss — found it losing 2.4psi in 5 minutes. Replaced the rubber O-rings in the tank and rechecked; no air leakage found. Rechecked the fluidics, which resolved both the fluidics issue and the violet laser issue. Performed baseline and performance tests for 100, 85, and 130 nozzles. System confirmed working properly under BD specifications and ready to use.

input.fault_description: Stream is unstable with all nozzles - ARIA III S/N P648282B3003. Stream is unstable with all nozzles
input.root_cause: Stream is moving down and and fsc ssc position shifts
input.work_performed:
November 10: It took a while to identify the issue. The stream position suddenly moved up and down. Replaced the ball seal and checked that there is no air leakage from the sample chamber. Replaced the sheath regulator. After replacing the sheath regulator, no stream instability was noticed. Calibrated the sample and sheath regulators for 3psi and 75psi, then started the sample flow rate adjustment but ran out of time.

November 11: Calibrated the sample flow rate, then had to recalibrate all optics. Cleaned the flow cell internally and externally and started aligning the optics. Ran a CST on nozzle 100 - violet laser CV was 5.6 (passed but not ideal). Noticed event rate with the 100 µm nozzle was high (~800 events), suspected this caused the high violet CV, and began recalibrating flow rate. Flow rate calibration was unstable and kept fluctuating.

November 12: Found the sample regulator was not operating properly - event rate jumped to ~2000 switching from nozzle 70 to 100, and dropped to ~350 after lowering the offset by 1. Reinstalled the original sheath regulator and replaced the sample regulator. Redid sample and sheath regulator calibration for 3psi and 75psi. Event rate fluctuated ±100 but sample rate calibration was completed. Stream was intermittently unstable again, and sometimes a loaded tube showed 0 events, requiring stopping and restarting the stream. Recalibrated optics after the flow rate calibration - all lasers aligned successfully except violet, which could not be calibrated below CV 6.5-6.8 despite adjusting the fiber manipulator position and rotating the fiber in the kinematic mount. Suspected the fluidics issue was affecting the violet laser.

November 18: Inflated the sheath tank and checked for pressure loss - found it was losing 2.4psi in 5 minutes. Replaced the rubber o-rings in the tank and confirmed no further air leakage. Rechecked the fluidics - this resolved both the fluidics issue and the violet laser issue. Performed baseline and performance tests for 100, 85, and 130 nozzles. System confirmed working properly under BD specifications and ready for use.

Privacy — this is not optional: never let the customer's name, account, address, phone number, contract number, or any other contact/billing detail enter a field's value, even in a text field, even when that detail sits on the same line or right next to text you do need. This also covers the engineer/technician's own name and the date they signed or logged an entry — quote logs are often written as "<note>. By <name> on <date>", and that attribution is not part of the fault, work, or note content any field is asking for. Crop tightly to only the content the field actually asks for. For example, a Subject line reading "11 Month Recurring / SMX0457374" contains a contract number after the slash — extract only "11 Month Recurring". Likewise a quote reading "Air bubble in bleach line. By Shachar on 18/04/2021" contains a technician sign-off — extract only "Air bubble in bleach line".

Separately from the template's fields, also give `report_date`: the date this service visit was carried out, as YYYY-MM-DD. This is the one date the record itself needs — the privacy rule above is about keeping dates out of *field values*, not about this. On a BD Care Work Order Service Report, take it from the LABOR table's Start/End Date And Time — the day the engineer actually worked on the instrument (if labor spans several days, use the last End date). If there is no labor table, use the date printed beside the signatures. Never use the service contract start/end dates, the PO date, or any date in the CALIBRATED TOOLS table — those describe the contract and the engineer's test equipment, not this visit.

BD forms are not consistent about day/month order: some print dates month-first (02/10/2026 is 10 February 2026), others day-first (18/04/2021 is 18 April 2021). Every date on one form uses the same order, so work it out from this form: any date on the page with a part greater than 12 settles it (03/17/2025 can only be month-first). If nothing on the form settles it, give your best reading and a `report_date__confidence` of 0.5 or lower. If no visit date appears on the form, use an empty string with a low confidence.

Fields to extract:
- fault_description (text) — reported symptom (BD's Subject line + Description)
- root_cause (text) — matches the form's own "Cause" section
- work_performed (text) — diagnostic/repair narrative ("Work Performed / Solution Comments")
- components_replaced (object[]) — one entry per part; mirrors the form's "Parts Used" table
- labor_hours (number, unit: hours) — rounded total from the form's "Labor" line
- fault_category (enum) — technician-assigned, not on the source form
- retest_result (enum) — technician-assigned, not on the source form

Suspected the fluidics issue was affecting the violet laser.

Rechecked the fluidics, which resolved both the fluidics issue and the violet laser issue. Performed baseline and performance tests for 100, 85, and 130 nozzles.
